_README: THE REGISTRANT BOUNDARY REGISTER -- every CIK a ticker's filings may come from.
A ticker's price history follows the ECONOMIC entity; its filings follow the LEGAL
registrant. When a company reorganises under a new holding company or re-registers in
another jurisdiction, the registrant's CIK changes and the price history does not.
`Company(ticker)` resolves exactly one CIK -- the one EDGAR's ticker table points at
TODAY -- so everything the predecessor filed becomes invisible with no error, no
exception and no gap signal. The ticker simply arrives with 22 filings where its peers
have 62, and nothing says why.
SEGMENTS, NOT TWO CIKs. `segments` is ordered oldest-first and CONTIGUOUS: the
`valid_from` of each segment equals the `valid_to` of the one before it, the oldest omits
`valid_from` and the newest omits `valid_to`. Chains are real -- PSKY is CBS -> Viacom ->
ViacomCBS -> Paramount Global -> Paramount Skydance -- and a two-CIK schema gives such a
ticker one hop and leaves the rest truncated.
A BOUNDARY IS `< valid_to` AND `>= valid_from`: strictly before / on-or-after. Adjacent
segments are therefore disjoint by construction rather than by de-duplication.
HOW THE SEGMENTS COMBINE IS A PROPERTY OF THE FORM, NOT OF THIS FILE. Event forms (8-K,
13D, 13G, Forms 3/4/5) take the UNION of every segment CIK; consolidating forms (10-K,
10-Q, DEF 14A) take the DATED SPLIT. Both rules are measured, and they are not
reconcilable into one: against APA's 2021-03-01 boundary the predecessor filed 4,291
Form 4s (4 after the boundary) and 140 10-K/10-Qs (15 after). A union of the event stream
gains 4,287 filings and risks 4; a union of the consolidating stream would blend 15
subsidiary 10-K/10-Qs into the parent's accounts -- a fuller-looking history that is
quietly wrong, which is the dangerous direction. See `common/registrant.FORM_POLICY`.
A RENAME IS NOT A CUTOVER AND BELONGS NOWHERE IN THIS FILE. CVS Caremark -> CVS Health
and Facebook -> Meta keep their CIK; an entry for either would walk one CIK twice and
duplicate every filing. `kind` may only be `reorganisation` or `domestication`, and the
loader rejects `kind: rename` BY NAME so the mistake cannot be made quietly. Sharadar
records a name change whether or not the CIK moved, which is exactly why the shell-name
evidence that motivates most entries here also fits a pure rename -- IVZ (AMVESCAP plc ->
Invesco) carries such an action and is NOT in this file, because CIK 914208 filed
continuously from 1994.
⚠ RISK ZONE. The failure mode is QUIET DATA LOSS: a `valid_to` set a year early drops the
predecessor's last four filings and admits nothing in their place, and nothing downstream
can tell that from a company that genuinely filed nothing. A wrong entry cannot raise on
its own, which is why every segment carries `evidence` and why the loader raises on every
malformed entry it CAN detect. Add an entry only with three oracles agreeing; see
`scripts/detect_registrant_cutovers.py`.
A curated JSON rather than an `sp500_tickers` column: that table is rebuilt from
Wikipedia, so a roster refresh would silently overwrite hand-established evidence. And
Wikipedia can itself be wrong in this exact way -- it had already moved XOM to the holdco.

segments.evidence: Apache Corp, the pre-2021 registrant. Measured against live EDGAR 2026-08-23: 125 10-K/10-Q filings before the boundary, 1994-03-21 .. 2021-02-26, 0 duplicate accessions and no gap -- the 2021-02-26 10-K is followed directly by the successor's 2021-05-07 10-Q. CRITICAL: Apache Corp KEPT FILING its own 10-K/10-Q through 2024-11-07 as a subsidiary with registered public debt, so those ~15 filings are correctly excluded by the dated split on consolidating forms and correctly ADMITTED by the union on event forms. It is the reference case for both rules.
APA Corp, the holding company created in the reorganisation effective 2021-03-01. 22 filings on or after the boundary (2021-05-07 ..) as measured 2026-08-23.

Apollo Asset Management Inc (CIK 0001411494) -- the entity FORMERLY named Apollo Global Management, renamed when the new parent took its name in the 2022 reorganisation. Found by the co-indexed filer scan; it filed 5 proxies of its own before the boundary and stopped filing 10-K/10-Q entirely at 2023-08-07 (51 filings, 2011-05-12 .. 2023-08-07, 0 after). BOUNDARY HAND-ADJUDICATED 2026-09-10 to 2022-05-10, the successor's first 10-Q, and NOT the 2023-08-08 the automatic rule proposed. ⚠ APO is the one register entry where both registrants filed a FULL quarterly consolidating series in parallel -- AAM 2022-05 .. 2023-08 at a 91-day median cadence alongside the new parent's own 92-day series -- so the generic 'day after the predecessor's last filing' rule would have kept AAM's 2022-2023 SUBSIDIARY accounts and excluded the parent's for five quarters, which is the blend the dated split exists to prevent. Oracle 4 fixes the date independently: the successor's first 10-K restates AAM's FY2021 as its comparative column (8 of 8 annual facts agree), so FY2022 is the first period the parent owns and the seam falls at Q1 2022. Contrast LIN and VTRS, where the successor's pre-boundary filings are SPARSE (3 filings over 12 months, and Upjohn carve-out reports respectively) and are correctly excluded instead.

HAND-ADJUDICATED 2026-09-10. BlackRock, Inc. -- the 1999 IPO registrant. EDGAR's own formerNames on CIK 0001060021 records exactly one prior name, 'BLACKROCK INC /NY', valid 1999-11-12 .. 2006-09-22; the entity is now named 'BlackRock Holdco 2, Inc.'. Its archive is 437 filings 1999-05-13 .. 2020-02-13, including 6 10-K (2000-03-28 .. 2006-03-08), 21 10-Q (1999-11-12 .. 2006-08-09), 45 8-K (1999-10-27 .. 2006-08-03) and 7 DEF 14A (2000-03-28 .. 2006-04-28); SIC 6282 Investment Advice, DE -- an operating registrant, not a shell. WHY THIS ONE: BLK prices start 1999-10-01 and this CIK's first 8-K is 1999-10-27 and its first 10-Q 1999-11-12, i.e. the IPO quarter, so it closes the whole pre-2006 hole that left BLK's 8-K history starting 2006-10-30. MECHANISM: the 2006 Merrill Lynch Investment Managers merger (announced 2006-02-15, closed ~2006-09-29) put a NEW holding company, 'New Boise, Inc.', over the business; New Boise became the listed BlackRock, Inc. = CIK 0001364742, whose archive starts 2006-11-14, and the original entity was renamed BlackRock Holdco 2. NOT CONFIRMED BY THE COMPARATIVE-COLUMN TEST: XBRL does not exist in 2006, so oracle 4 abstains -- this rests on EDGAR's formerNames transition plus the filing-cadence handover, NOT on an accounting-acquirer measurement. boundary = the day after the predecessor's LAST consolidating filing (10-Q, 2006-08-09), the same rule the 2024 segment uses. The gap to the successor's first filing (2006-11-14) contains no consolidating form, and EDGAR's rename date (2006-09-22) and the merger close both fall inside it, so the three candidate boundaries are indistinguishable for the dated split. Its 26 SC 13G/A run to 2007-02-15, AFTER the boundary -- kept by the UNION policy for event forms, which is what that policy is for. Found because --audit-chains flagged BLK's chain as incomplete.
